I’ve been using the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D for about two years now, and it’s been absolutely excellent—easily one of the best CPUs for gaming.
The performance is outstanding. Games run incredibly smooth, with high frame rates and great consistency, especially in CPU-heavy titles. The 3D V-Cache really makes a noticeable difference, giving it an edge in gaming compared to a lot of other processors. And it’s easy to install.
What really stands out is the price-to-performance ratio. You’re getting top-tier gaming performance without needing to spend on the most expensive flagship CPUs. It hits that perfect balance between power and value.
It’s also been very reliable and efficient. I haven’t had any issues over the past two years—no instability, no overheating problems when paired with a good cooler, and overall just a very solid experience.
Pros:
• One of the best CPUs for gaming
• Excellent price-to-performance value
• Smooth, consistent performance in demanding games
• Reliable over long-term use (2+ years)
• Efficient and easy to keep cool
Cons:
• Not the absolute best for heavy productivity compared to higher-core CPUs
Overall, if your main focus is gaming and you want a CPU that delivers top-tier performance without overspending, this is an easy recommendation. It’s compatible with all am5 motherboard

reviews.title: Outstanding gaming performance with excellent efficiency
reviews.comment:
The Ryzen 9800X3D has been an excellent upgrade and delivers exactly what it’s known for—top-tier gaming performance. Frame times are extremely consistent, CPU bottlenecks are minimal, and it performs exceptionally well in CPU-heavy games.
Despite the performance, power efficiency and thermals are very manageable compared to traditional high-end CPUs. With a decent cooler, temperatures stay under control even during long gaming sessions. Stability has been flawless with no crashes or issues.
While this CPU is clearly optimized for gaming, it still handles everyday productivity and multitasking smoothly. Pairing it with a solid AM5 motherboard and fast DDR5 memory makes a noticeable difference.
If gaming is your main priority, the 9800X3D is one of the best CPUs you can buy right now and is absolutely worth the investment.

reviews.title: Best Faming CPU For The $$ (Atm)
reviews.comment:
Such an amazing gaming CPU! This is my 2nd 3dv cache cpu, the first was the 7600x3d, and they are amazing for gaming. Some games you get insane gains, even at higher than 1080p resolution. 1080p will see the most gains.
Before buying the 7600x3d I had only ever bought intel. I decided to try the 3dv cache cpus to see what all the fuss was about and got a bundle from Micro Center. I am rocking the sane mobo I got with that bundle and the upgrade was drop in, reinstall the chipset drivers and I was good to go. If you've done any amount of research you will see the x3d chips have almost cornered the gaming market. Unless intel releases something drastically better, I see myself sticking with these 3dv cache cpus for a long time to come. What are you still reading for? Buy this gaming powerhouse!

reviews.title: Great CPU for a good price, excels at gaming.
reviews.comment: Built my first gaming PC in a few decades and decided to go with an AMD processor for the first time in my life. I've used Intel only since building my first PC in the mid 90's. Not saying I suddenly don't like Intel, but the price point and reviews of the X3D processors for gaming rigs really got my attention. I've been running this for about a year now and I'm very pleased with the performance at the price I paid. It's a CPU so if you've built a computer before you know you just carefully line it up in the socket and let it go, like the easiest install ever. I run it with a ThermalRight Grand Vision 360 AIO for cooling and my CPU temps sit pretty consistently under 45C during normal use, peaking around 67C while gaming (heavily modded Cyberpunk 2077 currently) most days. Under the heaviest loads I've put this through it has seen up to 72C.
